verdict.line: You lose if you let him land three autos or spells and trigger Darkness Rise mid-trade; you win if you poke with Rupture, bank Feast stacks, and let your health-stacking items take over after level 9.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's passive, Darkness Rise, only turns on after he lands three attacks or spells on a champion, so this lane is decided entirely by whether he gets sustained melee access to you. Cho'Gath's 950-range Q (Rupture) exists to poke and create distance before that threshold is reached, while any extended auto-trade hands Morde a free damage-and-speed buff he uses to close out the exchange. The head-to-head sits at 45.8% over 262 games with lane and solo-kill edge to Mordekaiser, which tracks with a kit built around punishing proximity rather than raw stat deficits.

theirWindow.when: he's landed 2 hits on you already
theirWindow.what: Disengage immediately rather than trading a third exchange — Darkness Rise gives him a damage aura and move speed on the third landed hit, and you cannot out-trade that buff in melee once it's live.

yourWindow.when: you land a clean Q knockup
yourWindow.what: Rupture's knock-up and slow buys you the full 950-range gap to walk away or follow with W (Feral Scream) from its 300-range cone; use the window to reset the poke pattern, not to walk back in and auto.

start.why: This is the majority start (72.8% pick, 48.3% win rate) and it fits the poke pattern — it fuels the mana cost of repeated Q/W pokes rather than rewarding the extended melee sustain that Doran's Shield is built for, which is exactly the trade you're trying to avoid.

boots.why: The majority pick (56.8%) at a near-identical win rate to Swiftness — the tenacity cuts the duration of his E (Death's Grasp) pull into a W (Feral Scream) silence chain, which is the exact combo that punishes you for standing still.

core.why: The strongest-performing sampled full build (56.3% over 16 games) starts here — it stacks health directly off your autos, compounding with Feast's permanent growth instead of competing with it.
Second item in that same top-performing path — adds sustain and AoE pressure once you're grouped, covering the window where his W (Indestructible) shield otherwise outlasts your damage.
Closes out the 56.3% win-rate path — the damage-reduction-into-healing effect directly counters the burst from his Q (Obliterate) hitting a single target.

situational.when: he's leaning on his W (Indestructible) self-heal to win extended trades
he's landing clean single-target Obliterate casts for burst damage
you want to pivot into the Riftmaker burst path instead of the tank bruiser build

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp's on-hit heal lets you absorb his early autos while you poke back with Q, directly offsetting the lane and solo-kill deficit this data shows, and it stacks the permanent health growth that's already central to your Feast identity.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (70.7%) at the dataset's best win rate (50.4%) — Teleport lets you reset after a poke-trade recall and still make level-advantage plays elsewhere, since you're not winning sustained pre-6 all-ins to justify Ignite.

playing.title: Poke, don't brawl
playing.detail: Lead every exchange with Q (Rupture, 9s cooldown, 950 range) from max range instead of walking into an auto-trade — every attack he lands on you in melee pushes him toward his passive threshold.

playing.title: Reset after two hits land
playing.detail: Darkness Rise triggers on his third landed attack or spell against you; if he's already connected twice, disengage rather than contest a third exchange.

playing.title: Save W for his engage tools
playing.detail: Feral Scream's silence (13s cooldown, 300-range cone) is more valuable shutting down his E (Death's Grasp) pull or his R cast than used purely for poke damage.

playing.title: Don't commit Feast carelessly
playing.detail: R (Feast, 60s cooldown) permanently grows you on a kill but costs half your stacks if you die — only cast it when the kill or your own survival is secured, since his W can bank the true damage you deal into a shield he turns into healing.

playing.title: Track his ultimate timer
playing.detail: Realm of Death starts at a 140s cooldown and isolates you 1v1, stealing your stats if he kills you — avoid overextending once enough time has passed for it to be back up.

playing.title: Hold Vorpal Spikes for forced trades
playing.detail: E's passive spike damage only matters once you're already in range, so don't walk in just to proc it — let it punish him when he initiates, not the other way around.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above reflect OP.GG's measured win rates for this matchup on the current patch (262 head-to-head games); the mechanical reasoning — when to poke, when to disengage, when to commit Feast — is my own read of the ability kit, not part of the stat sample.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to deactivate his (P) while using your skills to poke. Use [Q] to create some distance.
